title: HSYA targets the ZBP1-166R site to inhibit MAVS signaling: A potential therapeutic strategy for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
authors: Sun, Hao; Zhu, Kai; Peng, Yuqin; Zhou, Xian; Chang, Dennis; Wang, Ning; Huang, Ping
one_liner_zh: 该文研究HSYA靶向ZBP1-166R位点抑制MAVS信号通路以缓解脑缺血再灌注损伤，涉及蛋白-蛋白对接而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) is a marker of neuroinflammation caused by ischemic stroke. Hydroxylsafflower Yellow A (HSYA), the main active component of safflower, has neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke. Whether HSYA targets ZBP1 to protect mitochondrial function against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains unclear. METHODS: This study involves lateral ventricle injection of plasmid adeno-associated virus (AAV) targeting the ZBP1 locus in SD rats. The MCAO/R model is established using the line plug method to simulate CIRI. Laser speckle blood flow meter and TTC staining are used to evaluate the model. Behavioral, morphological, and imaging techniques were employed to assess the cerebro-protective effects of HSYA against CIRI. Protein-protein docking and co-immunoprecipitation (CO-IP) experiments confirmed the interaction between ZBP1 and MAVS. Subsequently, an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model was established in HT22 cells. The levels of inflammatory markers and ATP were measured using ELISA, and the expression of signaling pathway proteins was analyzed by Western blot. RESULTS: The cerebral blood flow in rats with a successfully established model was significantly decreased. HSYA reduces neurobehavioral scores and cerebral indices, improves ZBP1 pathologic distribution, and inhibits cell apoptosis. HSYA significantly enhanced cell viability and markedly decreased the apoptosis rate of cells following oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) treatment. Additionally, HSYA enhances mitochondrial function and suppresses inflammatory factor release by down-regulating ZBP1 and MAVS expression while up-regulating TBK1 expression, after MCAO/R injury. The protective effect of HSYA is weakened after ZBP1 site mutation. Moreover, ZBP1 and MAVS exhibit a significant interaction. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals the mechanism of HSYA resisting MCAO/R may be associated with ZBP1 - A166R locus, and to design new ZBP1 antagonist treatment of various diseases associated with ZBP1 provides a template.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：Z-DNA结合蛋白1（ZBP1）是缺血性卒中引起的神经炎症的标志物。羟基红花黄色素A（HSYA）是红花的主要活性成分，在缺血性卒中中具有神经保护作用。HSYA是否靶向ZBP1以保护线粒体功能对抗脑缺血再灌注损伤（CIRI）仍不清楚。方法：本研究涉及在SD大鼠侧脑室注射靶向ZBP1位点的质粒腺相关病毒（AAV）。采用线栓法建立MCAO/R模型以模拟CIRI。使用激光散斑血流仪和TTC染色评估模型。采用行为学、形态学和影像学技术评估HSYA对CIRI的脑保护作用。蛋白质-蛋白质对接和免疫共沉淀（CO-IP）实验确认了ZBP1与MAVS之间的相互作用。随后，在HT22细胞中建立氧糖剥夺/复氧（OGD/R）模型。使用ELISA测量炎症标志物和ATP水平，并通过Western blot分析信号通路蛋白的表达。结果：成功建立模型的大鼠脑血流量显著降低。HSYA降低神经行为评分和脑指数，改善ZBP1病理分布，并抑制细胞凋亡。HSYA显著增强细胞活力，并显著降低氧糖剥夺/复氧（OGD/R）处理后细胞的凋亡率。此外，在MCAO/R损伤后，HSYA通过下调ZBP1和MAVS表达同时上调TBK1表达，增强线粒体功能并抑制炎症因子释放。ZBP1位点突变后，HSYA的保护作用减弱。此外，ZBP1和MAVS表现出显著的相互作用。结论：我们的研究揭示了HSYA抵抗MCAO/R的机制可能与ZBP1-A166R位点相关，并为设计针对ZBP1相关多种疾病的新型ZBP1拮抗剂治疗提供了模板。
